newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Trade Ministry sees exports rising in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Trade Ministry sees exports rising in 1997.

text.p: Mexico's trade ministry hopes the country's exports will rise by 15 percent in 1997 over 1996, said Decio de Maria Serrano, deputy minister for foreign trade.

"The objective in 1997 exports is growth of 15 or 16 percent, which would would lift us to an export level greater than $100 billion," de Maria Serrano told reporters following a meeting with business leaders.
Mexico exported $95.929 billion worth of goods in 1996, up 20.6 percent over 1995.
"Exports have been performing in a satisfactory way," he said. "We closed the year meeting the objectives we had set."
From 1994 to 1996, the number of companies exporting goods from Mexico grew by one-third, he said.
"We closed the year with about 32,000 companies that exported at least once, and if you remeember in 1994 there were 24,000," he said.
The Trade Ministry would seek to increase the number of export companies even more in 1997, he said.
